author: aobolensk
title: CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race import_model called 4 times instead of expected 5
signature: Actual function call count doesnt match EXPECT_CALL import_model Expected called times Actual called times unsatisfied and active|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: C++ unit tests / C++ unit tests

key_errors:
caching_test.cpp(2667): error: Actual function call count doesn't match EXPECT_CALL(*mockPlugin, import_model(A<std::istream&>(), _))...
         Expected: to be called 5 times
           Actual: called 4 times - unsatisfied and active
root_cause: The LoadMultiWithConfig_race test is a race-condition stress test that loads models concurrently and asserts a specific number of import_model calls (5 for ByModelName). Due to inherent timing non-determinism, the actual call count fluctuates between runs — the test got 4 instead of 5. The PR changes only src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/emitters/plugin/riscv64/jit_emitter.cpp (RISC-V64 CPU emitter), which is completely unrelated to the caching/multi-device load path tested here.
reproduction_steps: Run: ov_inference_functional_tests --gtest_filter="CachingTest/CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race/ByModelName_testCache" on Windows — fails intermittently due to race timing.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed job — this is a known flaky race-condition test
Re-add PR #37187 to the merge queue if it was dropped
prevention_strategies: Consider increasing the retry tolerance or stabilizing the expected call count range in LoadMultiWithConfig_race tests to reduce flakiness.
historical_context: This CachingTest race failure pattern is new in the database but is a known category of flaky tests in the OpenVINO caching infrastructure tests.
